source.title: Why there are complementary learning systems in the hippocampus and neocortex: insights from the successes and failures of connectionist models of learning and memory

confidence_rationale: Foundational, heavily-replicated CLS account. Directly establishes that integrating new knowledge into a single shared (cortical-analogue) representation REQUIRES gradual interleaved training; non-interleaved focused learning produces catastrophic interference rather than integration. Maps cleanly onto MECH-423's readiness precondition (R3: offline interleaving must be active) but is a necessary-condition argument about WHEN integration helps, not a direct measurement of super-additivity in REE -- hence mapping_fidelity capped below 0.8.
failure_signatures: If the integrated arm trains all modules in a focused, non-interleaved schedule (one module's experience swept before the next), the shared latent suffers catastrophic interference and integrated performance falls BELOW a modular baseline -- a sub-additive result that is an artefact of the missing interleaving prerequisite, not evidence against super-additivity.

Structure discovery (the source of any cross-module gain) only emerges when learning of each item is gradual and interleaved with learning about other items; a single-pass or blocked schedule yields no shared structure to be super-additive over.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Connectionist (shared-weight) systems discover the structure latent in an ensemble of experiences only if learning is gradual and interleaved across items; the hippocampus exists precisely to support this by replaying experiences so neocortex can integrate them slowly without catastrophic interference.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-423's super-additive gain depends on a shared L-space latent (ARC-004) integrating E1/E2/object-spine experience. CLS says that integration is only realisable when an offline interleaving engine (REE's MECH-121 replay / sleep consolidation) is actively moving traces across modules. This is the literature backbone for readiness condition R3 -- 'offline/consolidation transfer must be active' -- and explains why, below it, integrated approximately equals isolated by construction.
mapping.mapping_caveat: CLS is about avoiding interference during sequential learning, not specifically about gains EXCEEDING the additive baseline. It grounds the necessity of the interleaving prerequisite, but a positive super-additive margin in REE is an additional claim CLS does not itself establish. Connectionist-cortex analogy to REE's L-space is structural, not identity.
mapping.source_context: Connectionist simulations of human/animal memory; hippocampal-neocortical division of labour; catastrophic interference in backprop networks.

confidence_components.notes: Canonical paper, thousands of citations, repeatedly validated. Weighted down on mapping because it argues necessity of interleaving, not the super-additive magnitude MECH-423 asserts; transfer risk moderate (connectionist-to-REE-substrate analogy is close but not identity).
